_comments: bc-aidp-next-golive#226 item 3: Contract ID and Renews Contract ID rendered as raw GUIDs in
text boxes with no link. The cause is structural, not cosmetic. Both columns are SOFT
references — their own column descriptions say so — because the link points DOWN the
dependency graph and contracts knows nothing about sales. No database FK means CodeGen sets no
RelatedEntityID, and mj-form-field with no related entity has no name to show and nowhere to
go, so it falls back to printing the id.
MJ's answer to exactly this is a SOFT FOREIGN KEY: RelatedEntityID + RelatedEntityFieldName
with IsSoftForeignKey=1, which is what protects the pair from being cleared by the next schema
sync (AutoUpdateRelatedEntityInfo=0 is the other half — it tells CodeGen this is ours, not
something to re-derive from a constraint that does not exist).
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it creates no constraint, no cascade, and nothing to violate. The
database is untouched. A contract can still be deleted out from under a deal exactly as it
could yesterday — the shared chip row and mj-form-field both already handle an id that names
no row, by showing nothing rather than a dead link.
Contracts is a declared dependency in mj-app.json, so naming its entity here is legitimate. The
matching declaration in codegen-schema-info.json is what re-applies this on every rebuild, and
it SKIPS with a warning on a host where contracts is absent rather than failing.
The renewal chain's other end. Same soft reference, same reason, and this is the one a REP
types: DealType.RequiresRenewalSource makes it mandatory on a renewal deal, and until now the
only way to fill it was to paste a UUID. With the related entity set, mj-form-field offers an
FK search instead.
